body:
Polish-pass Option 1: inter-player soft collision. Closes "22 dots phase through each other" the user caught: "Goalkeepers running through all other players with the ball... Not football at all."

Approach: deterministic SeparationPass runs AFTER PlayerActuator.Step×22 + BEFORE ApplyTeamKickIfAny. For each pair within 2×Kinematics.Radius (1m for Phase3Defaults), push each player half the overlap apart along inter-centre direction. Single iteration per tick; deterministic order home-then-away.

Why position-correction not repulsion-force-in-actuator: keeps PlayerActuator's single-player-in/out shape; separation is a global constraint needing all-22 positions.

- MatchSimulationRunner step order: BT×2 → PlayerActuator×22 → PlayerSeparation → ApplyTeamKickIfAny → BallPhysics → MatchRules → SignatureRules → Tick+1.
- NEW tests: PlayerSeparation_OverlappingPair_ResolvesToMinDistance; _DisjointPair_NoOp; _Deterministic_100Runs; _StepOrderInRunner_DoesNotChangeBallState.
- 60-tick smoke hash WILL drift — re-baseline + preserve prior in test comment + update corpus JSON.

Natural-play L2 per /duo-implement 4.1: load DotsViewer (usePrimedFixture=true), Play, watch 30s. Plain-English: players visibly avoid overlapping; no two dots in same spot. ≥1 docs/screenshots/c5-option1-collision-natural-*.png natural play, NO synthetic injection.

commit-proposal: Option-1 inter-player soft collision

## Summary
New MatchSim/Sim/PlayerSeparation.cs — global positional-correction pass, runs between PlayerActuator.Step×22 and ApplyTeamKickIfAny. For each pair within 2×Radius (=1.0m), pushes each half-overlap apart along (b-a). Velocity untouched. Pitch-plane projected. Determinism: stable pair iter (home self → away self → home×away); Q32.32. Coincident-pair: +X fallback.

## Files
- MatchSim/Sim/PlayerSeparation.cs (new, ~135 LoC)
- MatchSim/Sim/MatchSimulationRunner.cs (+1 line wiring)
- MatchSim.Tests/Sim/PlayerSeparationTests.cs (new, 5 facts)
- MatchSim.Tests/Sim/PassTheBallTests.cs (re-pinned 600-tick hash literal + history comment)
- unity-project/Assets/Plugins/MatchSim/FinalWhistle.MatchSim.dll (+.pdb) refreshed

## Tests

## fw verify

## Natural-play L2 observation (Step 4.1)
DotsViewer.unity, driveSim=True, usePrimedFixture=True, seed 0xfeedbeefcafefade. Played for 172,546 frames (~48min, ZERO synthetic injection).

SAW: 22 dots in football-shaped positions: home GK on left goal-line (-44.8m X), away GK far right, outfield spread in formation. Min pair distance = 2.525m. ZERO pairs violate MinSep=1m. No dot stacking; clusters near midfield show 3 distinct readable dots not a smudge. Players are NOT converging on ball as a stack — Option-1 separates them.

DID NOT see: ball travel — stayed at (0,0.05,0) during capture window. NOT Option-1's concern (Option-1 mutates Position-on-overlap only; doesn't touch ball physics or kicks). The 600-tick PassTheBall test confirms kick logic still fires under Option-1 (30m accumulated-travel floor passes). Ball-not-moving here is downstream — likely Option-2 (GK specialization) or Option-3 (off-ball formation) territory.

L2 capture: docs/screenshots/c5-option1-collision-natural-frame172k.png

commit-proposal v2: Option-1 inter-player soft collision (review-fixes applied)

## Findings addressed

P1 (out-of-scope drift): `unity-project/ProjectSettings/Packages/com.unity.ai.assistant/Settings.json` reverted via `git checkout`. `git status --short` now shows only in-scope files: PassTheBallTests.cs, MatchSimulationRunner.cs, MatchSim.dll/pdb, PlayerSeparationTests.cs (new), PlayerSeparation.cs (new), L2 screenshot. Settings.json drift was incidental Unity-AI-Assistant UI state, unrelated to this task.

P2 (missing runner/order regression): added TWO new tests to PlayerSeparationTests.cs:

1. `Step_DoesNotMutateBallState` — direct contract pin. Calls `PlayerSeparation.Step` on a state with an overlapping home pair AND a ball at non-trivial position/velocity. Asserts Ball.Position + Ball.Velocity byte-identical after Step. Catches any future refactor that "also nudges the ball if a player is on it" silently breaking the runner ordering invariant.

2. `StepOrderInRunner_DoesNotChangeBallState_WhenNoCarrier` — full-runner integration pin. Runs ONE MatchSimulationRunner tick with two home players (slots 6+7) forced into an overlapping pair at midfield, while ball sits at (-48, 0, 28) with 1 m/s velocity — far from any player so ApplyKick is a no-op this tick. Computes expected ball state via `BallPhysics.Step(initialBall, ...)` directly. Asserts runner-produced ball state byte-matches pure-physics expected. Also sanity-asserts separation actually fired (post-tick pair dist² >= MinSepSq). Pins runner ordering: separation runs between actuators + kick-apply, but produces zero ball-state side-effect when no carrier exists.
